active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.medfilt with adaptive window for edge-preserving smoothing
active_paradigms.description: Replace Wiener filter with scipy.signal.medfilt which uses median-based filtering instead of mean-based. Median filtering is more robust to outliers and preserves signal edges better, directly reducing false reversals and slope changes. Implement adaptive window sizing based on local signal variance - use smaller windows in low-variance regions for responsiveness and larger windows in high-variance regions for noise reduction. The median filter naturally handles the non-stationary characteristics of the test signals better than linear filters. This approach targets the 60% combined penalty from slope changes and false reversals.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (30% weight) and false reversal penalty (30% weight) by preserving genuine trend changes while filtering noise-induced reversals
active_paradigms.cautions: Median filter output length may differ from input - ensure proper alignment with evaluator's delay calculation. Window size must be odd. Test different window sizes (5, 7, 9) to find optimal trade-off between smoothness and responsiveness.

active_paradigms.idea: Implement hysteresis-based trend confirmation to eliminate false reversals
active_paradigms.description: After initial filtering (using any base filter), apply a hysteresis mechanism that only confirms a trend change after the new direction persists for N consecutive samples. Track the current trend state (up/down/flat) and require sustained evidence before switching states. This directly addresses the false reversal penalty which compares filtered signal trend changes against clean signal. Implement using numpy arrays to count consecutive samples in same direction before confirming a reversal. This post-processing step can be combined with any base filter to reduce R(θ) penalty without affecting other metrics significantly.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversal penalty R(θ) (30% weight) by preventing noise-induced spurious direction changes that don't match the clean signal
active_paradigms.cautions: Hysteresis threshold N must be tuned carefully - too high causes lag, too low allows false reversals. Typical range 3-7 samples. Must account for the evaluator's delay calculation when aligning filtered signal with clean signal for comparison.

active_paradigms.idea: Use double exponential smoothing (Holt's method) for better trend tracking
active_paradigms.description: Implement Holt's double exponential smoothing which tracks both level and trend components separately, providing better responsiveness to genuine signal changes than Wiener filter. Use two smoothing parameters: alpha for level (0.1-0.3) and beta for trend (0.05-0.15). This method naturally reduces lag error while maintaining smoothness, addressing the 40% combined penalty from lag and tracking error. The trend component allows the filter to anticipate direction changes rather than just react to them. Implement using numpy array operations for efficiency.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lag error (20% weight) and average tracking error (20% weight) by better tracking genuine signal trends while maintaining responsiveness
active_paradigms.cautions: Two parameters (alpha, beta) need tuning for optimal performance. Different test signals may require different parameter values. Ensure causal implementation (only use past data) for real-time compatibility. Initialize level and trend from first few samples carefully.

tried_paradigms.description: Replace the weighted moving average with Savitzky-Golay filter, which fits a polynomial to data within each sliding window using least squares. This preserves signal shape and derivatives better than simple averaging, directly reducing slope change penalties. The polynomial fitting maintains genuine trend changes while smoothing noise, addressing both S(θ) and R(θ) metrics. Use window_size matching the input parameter and polynomial order of 2-3 for optimal trade-off between smoothness and tracking. This approach is fundamentally different from mean-based filtering as it models local signal structure rather than just averaging.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope change penalty (S), false reversal penalty (R), and tracking accuracy through polynomial structure preservation
tried_paradigms.cautions: Ensure polynomial order is less than window_size, handle edge cases properly, and choose order 2-3 for good balance between smoothness and responsiveness

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.wiener for adaptive local statistics filtering
tried_paradigms.description: Implement Wiener filter which adapts to local signal statistics rather than using fixed weights. The filter estimates local mean and variance within a window and applies optimal linear filtering based on signal-to-noise ratio. This directly minimizes tracking error (L_avg) by adapting to signal characteristics. Unlike the current exponential weighting, Wiener filter responds to actual signal volatility, reducing both lag error and false reversals. Use the window_size parameter to control adaptation range and let the filter automatically determine optimal smoothing based on local variance estimates.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Tracking error (L_avg), lag error (L_recent), and adaptive response to signal volatility
tried_paradigms.cautions: Wiener filter assumes locally stationary statistics within window, may need to tune window size for best results, ensure signal has sufficient length for variance estimation

tried_paradigms.idea: Implement Kalman filter with state-space estimation using numpy
tried_paradigms.description: Build a Kalman filter that models the signal as a state-space system with process and measurement noise. The filter uses prediction-correction cycle: predict next state based on previous state and dynamics, then correct using new measurement. This provides optimal estimation for linear Gaussian systems, naturally balancing smoothness and tracking. The Kalman gain automatically adjusts based on estimated noise levels, providing adaptive filtering without fixed weights. Implement with state vector [position, velocity] to capture trend, reducing lag through predictive capability and minimizing false reversals through probabilistic state estimation.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: All metrics simultaneously through optimal Bayesian estimation, especially lag error (L_recent) and tracking accuracy through predictive capability
tried_paradigms.cautions: Initialize covariance matrices properly, tune process and measurement noise parameters, ensure numerical stability with matrix operations

tried_paradigms.description: Replace the Wiener filter with Savitzky-Golay filter which fits a polynomial to each sliding window using least squares. This preserves higher-order signal features like peaks and slopes while smoothing noise. Use window_length=21 (odd, larger than current 20) and polyorder=3 for cubic polynomial fitting. The filter naturally reduces slope changes and false reversals by maintaining signal dynamics. Unlike Wiener which only considers local variance, Savitzky-Golay preserves the shape of the signal better.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S), false reversals (R), and tracking accuracy (correlation)
tried_paradigms.cautions: Window length must be odd and greater than polynomial order. Edge effects may occur at signal boundaries. Polyorder=3 is good balance between smoothness and feature preservation.

tried_paradigms.description: Apply exponential smoothing with exponentially decaying weights to recent observations. This minimizes lag error by giving higher weight to recent samples while still smoothing noise. Configure with trend='add' and seasonal=None for non-seasonal signals. The smoothing parameter alpha (typically 0.2-0.4) controls responsiveness vs smoothness tradeoff. This approach adapts better to non-stationary signals than fixed-window filters.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and tracking accuracy
tried_paradigms.cautions: Initial values may cause edge effects. Alpha too high increases noise sensitivity, too low increases lag. Works best for signals with gradual changes rather than abrupt jumps.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use Hampel filter combining scipy.signal.medfilt and scipy.stats.mad for outlier removal
tried_paradigms.description: Implement Hampel filter which detects outliers using median absolute deviation (MAD) and replaces them with local median. First compute local median using medfilt with kernel_size=11, then calculate MAD of residuals. Replace values where |signal - median| > k * MAD (k=3.0 typical) with the local median. This is robust to outliers that create false reversals while preserving genuine signal structure better than simple median filtering.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) and slope changes (S) by removing noise-induced outliers
tried_paradigms.cautions: Hampel filter is more aggressive on outliers than smoothing filters. May smooth genuine sharp transitions if threshold k is too low. Works best when outliers are sparse relative to signal length.
